meta.title: Four Stars for the Old Town Walk
meta.textType: functional: a review with stars and reasons, for the class blog

paragraphs: Posted by Leo. On Saturday, February thirteenth, the Explorers went on a walk in the old town. We took the bus at a quarter past eight, and we walked for two hours. Today is Monday, and this is my review of the walk. Lily checks every post for our blog, so she stood behind me and read this post over my shoulder. Teacher Kim reads each post after Lily, and then this post went online. Before the walk, I thought, "I will be bored," but I was wrong. Lily smiled when she read that, because I am almost never wrong.

Here are my stars for three places on the walk. The old gate gets five stars. The gallery gets five stars, too. The tea shop gets only two stars. Twelve stars for three places is four stars for each place. So the whole walk gets four stars in all. I give a reason for each star, because a review without reasons is only a shout.

I liked the old gate especially, because it was awesome to touch the old stone. Mia found the number on the stone, and it was eighteen twenty. The gallery was interesting, too. Playing a video game is my favorite hobby, but the old photos were better. Is a video game better than a real place? Here is my cartoon of that. In the cartoon, I hold a game controller in one hand. With the other hand, I point at the old gate. I say one word: "Real!"

The tea shop gets only two stars, because the children waited twenty minutes for juice. It was crowded, and the people in the line were not happy. I counted the people in front of us, and there were nine. I hate waiting, and that wait was horrible. At last, the juice came, and it was cold and sweet. Even so, two stars is fair.

The walk had other good things. The program was useful, because it had a key and the time of every stop. The weather was perfect for walking. The bus ride was short, and the driver was kind. Walking for two hours was easy, because my shoes were comfortable.

Lily read my post twice, and she said, "Your reasons are clear." This is not an ad. It is my opinion. Would you go? I think you should, because the old town is real. Which place would you give five stars?
text.summary: Leo writes a review of the old town walk for the class blog. He gives stars to three places, and he gives a reason for each star, so the walk gets four stars in all.
